words.meaning: arising from within the system or situation being studied
words.example: The analysis treats stronger customer loyalty as an endogenous result of the service improvements.

words.meaning: the degree to which one product, resource, or service can replace another
words.example: The low substitutability of that component gives its only supplier considerable leverage.

words.meaning: moving in the opposite direction from the broader economic or business cycle
words.example: Repair services can be countercyclical because people fix older equipment when budgets tighten.

words.meaning: a cost or benefit of an activity that affects people who were not directly involved in it
words.example: Extra traffic near the warehouse is an externality that the expansion plan needs to address.

words.meaning: not changing at a constant rate or following a simple straight-line pattern
words.example: Support demand grew in a nonlinear way once the customer base passed ten thousand users.

phrases.meaning: done using whatever methods or resources are available, without a settled plan
phrases.example: Until the new coordinator starts, scheduling will be catch as catch can.

phrases.meaning: to do everything possible or include every available feature and detail
phrases.example: For the flagship store, the designers went the whole nine yards with custom lighting and displays.

phrases.term: make a mountain out of a molehill
phrases.meaning: to make a minor problem seem much more serious than it really is
phrases.example: One typo is easy to fix, so let's not make a mountain out of a molehill.

phrases.meaning: to act with serious intent because the outcome has lasting consequences
phrases.example: Once the larger firms entered the market, everyone knew they were playing for keeps.

phrases.meaning: to greatly outperform someone or exceed expectations by a wide margin
phrases.example: The new campaign blew the doors off our previous signup record in its first week.
